items.title: AI literacy interventions in education: A meta-analysis of effects and moderators

findings.claim: Bibliographic dates: received 2025-10-27, revised 2026-05-29, accepted 2026-06-27, available online 2026-07-02; ScienceDirect browser agent also reported Version of Record 2026-07-03; volume 52, August 2026, article 100813. CUHK repository lists 'Published - Aug 2026'. First-public of any preprint not searched/verified.
findings.evidence_quote_short: Received 27 October 2025; ... Accepted 27 June 2026 ... Available online 2 July 2026
findings.confidence: high for online/accepted/received (two independent reads: RG copy of article front matter and ScienceDirect browser agent); medium for Version of Record 2026-07-03 (browser agent only)

findings.claim: School-level distribution of the 59 included studies is elementary 12 (32 effect sizes), secondary 20 (68 ES), higher education 23 (63 ES), mixed 4 (9 ES). Secondary is NOT split into lower/upper secondary. Higher education is the largest group (38.98%); so the pool is not K-12 only (K-12 elementary+secondary = 32 of 59 studies).
findings.evidence_quote_short: most studies targeted higher education (n = 23, 38.98%) and secondary school students (n = 20, 33.90%)
findings.confidence: high (article Section 4 text and Table of subgroup results read in extracted full text; elementary/mixed counts also from Table; browser agent concurred)

findings.claim: Educational level is a non-significant moderator: F(3,168)=1.174, p=.321. Mixed-level subgroup is descriptively largest (g=1.041, k=9 ES) but flagged by authors as cautious; secondary g=0.663, higher ed g=0.952, elementary g=0.845. No stage-based superiority can be claimed.
findings.evidence_quote_short: No significant differences in effect sizes were found across educational levels (F (3, 168) = 1.174, p =.321)

findings.claim: Included designs: inclusion required '(quasi-)experimental designs'; effect sizes were computed for both independent-groups posttest designs and single-group pretest-posttest designs (Hedges' g, three-level model). Single-group pre-post are not controlled comparisons; they were pooled with controlled posttest designs. Eight outlying effect sizes excluded; with them retained the pooled estimate was larger (g=1.270).
findings.evidence_quote_short: calculated for both independent-groups posttest designs and single-group pretest-posttest designs

findings.claim: Bias / quality assessment: no formal risk-of-bias tool is described in the text searched; authors state study quality was not incorporated into weighting and that varying internal validity may have contributed to variation. The review was not preregistered. Absence of a tool was established by keyword search of the extracted body (first 100000 chars) plus the browser agent's page search, not by a line-by-line audit of the Methods; cautiously 'not found', not 'confirmed none'.
findings.evidence_quote_short: study quality was not explicitly incorporated into the weighting

findings.claim: Effect-size scope: overall g=0.837 (p<.001), 59 studies, 172 ES, 7211 participants, 95% prediction interval [-0.292, 1.966] crossing zero; authors state effects may not generalize uniformly. Significant moderators only region and learning-outcome focus; larger descriptive effects for mixed/reflective pedagogy, GenAI tools, performance tasks are non-significant. Outcomes are mostly AI knowledge (46 of the coded outcomes), instruments include self-report (44.87%) and performance tasks (52.56%). Not a universal K-12 or causal-superiority finding.
findings.evidence_quote_short: may not generalize uniformly across contexts

findings.claim: Search scope: authors restricted to English peer-reviewed journal articles and conference proceedings; included studies published 2020-2024 (with 2024 n=28, 47.46%); participants must be students. So K-12 relevance is limited to the elementary and secondary subgroups; it would be wrong to relabel the pooled effect as K-12.
findings.evidence_quote_short: published between 2020 and 2024, with a notable increase in 2024 (n = 28, 47.46%)

remaining_gaps: Primary vs lower-secondary vs upper-secondary split is not reported (single 'Secondary' code); Appendix A per-study table could allow manual recount but was only partially read (first part of 100000 chars).

Formal risk-of-bias tool absence not line-audited; ScienceDirect direct crawl via Exa HTTP 400, full text read via ResearchGate copy (provenance of RG PDF = article front matter shows ScienceDirect header; treated as the published version but not verified as publisher PDF).
Earliest preprint / first public version not searched (publisher online 2026-07-02 only).
Version of Record 2026-07-03 reported by cloud-browser agent summary only.
proposed_kb_changes: Set publisher_online date 2026-07-02 (day precision), issue Aug 2026 vol 52 art. 100813; mark first_publication still online-first not global earliest.

Add scope note: 'meta-analysis of AI literacy interventions across elementary (12), secondary (20), higher education (23), mixed (4) studies; not K-12 only; includes single-group pre-post; no formal RoB tool found; prediction interval crosses zero'.
Keep content_checked unpromoted unless the integrator accepts the RG-text read; claim wording must not say 'K-12 effect g=0.837'.

items.title: Day of AI Australia: Teacher Insights from a Nation-Wide AI Literacy Program for K-12 Students

findings.claim: Dates: ACM publication date 2025-02-18; poster session at SIGCSE TS 2025 on Fri 28 Feb 2025, 15:00-17:00, Exhibit Hall C Posters #3; conference 26 Feb-1 Mar 2025, Pittsburgh. ACM Publication History shows a single entry (browser agent). Type Poster, 2 pages (pp. 1375-1376 per browser agent), proceedings V.2. No earlier public version found (not exhaustively searched).
findings.evidence_quote_short: Published: 18 February 2025
findings.confidence: high for ACM date and event date (two sources: ACM page via Exa, SIGCSE event page); medium for pages 1375-1376 (browser agent only)

findings.claim: Instrument/sample (from poster text via browser agent): per-lesson anonymous teacher feedback in the Day of AI Australia learning management system, 5-point Likert (1 Strongly Disagree to 5 Strongly Agree) on student knowledge change, lesson appropriateness and likelihood to teach again; 61 teachers responded, representing about 2,946 students; whole program 64,000 students and 370 teachers. This is teacher-perceived student knowledge change, not student assessment.
findings.evidence_quote_short: 61 teachers responded to the forms
findings.confidence: medium (single cloud-browser read of the ACM ePDF; output is an agent paraphrase with short quotes, not independently confirmed; 61 is consistent with the abstract's 'over 60')

findings.claim: School level: upper primary and early secondary (ages 10 to 16) per abstract (official SIGCSE page and ACM page).
findings.evidence_quote_short: upper primary and early secondary school (ages 10 to 16)

findings.claim: Limitations reported (via browser agent): 89.7% of students from Major cities; Independent and Catholic schools over-represented; data only available as high-level aggregations to protect teacher anonymity. Evidence is teacher feedback on a national program; no student-level outcomes, no comparison group.
findings.evidence_quote_short: 89.7% of students came from Major cities

remaining_gaps: Poster body read only through a cloud-browser agent summary; exact quotes and the numbers (61, 2,946, 64,000, 370, 89.7%) should be re-read from the ePDF by a second reader before use in public text.
No direct Exa/WebFetch read of poster PDF (HTML only). Local original poster file not obtained.
Earlier non-ACM public versions (Day of AI Australia site, UNSW) not searched in depth.
proposed_kb_changes: Fill dates: ACM publication 2025-02-18 (publisher_online, day), conference_event 2025-02-28 poster session, type poster, 2 pages, region Australia, level upper primary/early secondary ages 10-16.
Add scope: teacher post-lesson Likert feedback (n=61 of 370 teachers), no student outcome measurement; do not use as evidence of student efficacy.
Keep partial until second-reader confirmation of the PDF numbers.

items.title: Teaching Machine Learning to Senior Primary Students: Evaluating a Course for AI Literacy in a Hong Kong Primary School

findings.claim: Design: six-hour ML course with AlphAI robots; convenience sample of 145 sixth-grade students (94 boys, 51 girls; ages 10-13; M=10.94) from five classes in ONE primary school; pre/post 13-item concept test (Cronbach alpha 0.656) plus five focus groups of three students (15 students). No comparison or control group is described anywhere in the extracted paper.
findings.evidence_quote_short: convenience sample of 145 sixth-grade students
findings.confidence: high (full extracted PDF text read: abstract, sections 1-5, references)

findings.claim: Matched-analysis denominator: the paper never states the number of pre/post pairs analysed. 145 is the recruited/consented sample; the Wilcoxon result (Z=5.860, pre M=5.03 SD=2.072 to post M=7.07 SD=2.790, p<.001) and the boys/girls Mann-Whitney (U=1769.50) have no N reported. Missing data, attrition, absences, and handling of incomplete pairs are not mentioned. Matched N therefore remains unknown; do not write 'n=145 matched'.
findings.confidence: high that N matched and missing-data info are absent from the extracted text; medium that nothing is lost in extraction (no page images)

findings.claim: Paper type: ICCE 2025 proceedings article in the main proceedings; PDF header 'Proceedings of the 33rd ICCE'; the text is short (about 4-6 printed pages by length; page count not shown in extraction) and the APSCE page and EdUHK repository do not label it full/short/workshop. Full vs short therefore unverified.
findings.evidence_quote_short: Published - 2025
findings.confidence: medium for 'type unlabelled', high that label could not be found

findings.claim: Dates: APSCE article page and issue page show Published 2025-12-01 (issue/proceedings volume); ICCE 2025 held 1-5 December 2025 in Chennai (main conference from 3 Dec). 2025-12-01 is the proceedings publication stamp and coincides with the first day of the conference; presentation day of this paper not established. Pre-event versions not found.
findings.evidence_quote_short: Published: 2025-12-01
findings.confidence: high for 2025-12-01 stamp; presentation date unknown

findings.claim: Conclusion language overstates ('demonstrated the effectiveness') relative to design; authors themselves note limited generalisability due to small sample and one school. Pre-post gain in a one-group design cannot support causal attribution or Hong Kong-wide generalisation. A companion teacher-focus-group paper (IATED ICERI 2025, Yang, Chow, Kong) is a different study with 16 teachers, not the same data.
findings.evidence_quote_short: generalisability of this study is limited by its small sample size

remaining_gaps: Matched pre/post N, missing data/attrition: not reported in the paper (unknown, not zero).
Full vs short paper status unlabelled; page count not seen.
Presentation date within ICCE 2025 unknown; possible earlier preprint not searched.
Read via extracted text, not page images.
